research_period: Milan, Paris and Pitti Uomo menswear shows, June 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Global: Milan, Paris and Florence runways; premium and mid-market menswear
title: SS27 Men's Tender Masculinity
summary: Softness, sensuality and decoration in menswear: nude and aquamarine tones, lingerie references, organza feathers and floral satins.

sections.heading: The story
sections.body: Menswear embraced softness and sensuality in Paris: Dries Van Noten showed sensual silhouettes in nude and aquamarine tones and Egonlab lingerie-inspired ensembles<sup>[1]</sup>. Patrick Clark, fashion editor at GQ France, called the season "a confirmation of the crossover between the men's and women's wardrobes"<sup>[1]</sup>. At Pitti Uomo, Simone Rocha's first men's show used boas of organza feathers, cornflower-blue embellishment, aprons and pinafores, under the theme "tender masculinity"<sup>[2]</sup>. Willy Chavarria showed floral satin sets<sup>[3]</sup>, and Thom Browne put pleated skirts on men in Milan<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: Salmon pink, butter and ice blue, with nude and aquamarine tones. See SS27 Men's Season Colours.

sections.heading: Silhouettes
sections.body:
- Fluid shirts and trousers; floral satin sets.
- Skirts and aprons layered over trousers (fashion customers).
- Soft, unstructured jackets.

sections.heading: Fabrics
sections.body: Satin, including floral satin<sup>[3]</sup>; organza; sheer cottons; fine knits.

sections.heading: Trims and details
sections.body: Embroidered florals, organza feathers<sup>[2]</sup>, brooches, beading.

timing: In stores February to July 2027. An emerging direction: test with fashion customers; Forecut expects softer colour and fabric to reach the mainstream before skirts do.
products: - Satin shirts and sets; embroidered shirts; soft-coloured knitwear; skirts and aprons for fashion customers.
design_implications:
- Introduce softness through colour and fabric first (satin, pastel knits).
- Keep construction masculine where the customer needs it: shoulders, collars, trouser blocks.
commercial_implications:
- Small buys for skirts and aprons; build depth in satin shirts and soft-coloured knits.
- Merchandise by mood, not by gender, for fashion stores and online.
